params.body:
The same forward was kept twice. mail:4 (received 05:59) and mail:1 (06:06) are one forwarded mail: the first attempt, made before receiving was configured, was delivered later by Resend's retry under another id. Each became a mail, and the workbench would have taken both up.

- **Each mail now carries a fingerprint:** sender, subject, the owner's instruction and the forwarded text. A forward with the same fingerprint on the same project within a day is the mail already kept, and Portal answers with that mail (`duplicate: true`). The same mail forwarded with **another instruction** is another request, and another mail.
- **A migration** gives the stored mails their fingerprint. A later copy of an earlier one, if still `new`, is closed as `done` with the note "the same forward as mail:N". It keeps the first one **stored** (the lowest id), not the one with the earliest time, because a session may already be working on it. Here that closes mail:4 and keeps mail:1.

## Tests

- `ForwardedMailTest` grows by 1: a second delivery of the same forward is the first mail; another instruction makes a new one.
- The migration was run by hand on SQLite with three mails: two copies of one forward, the later-stored one carrying the earlier time, and a third mail. It kept id 1, closed id 2 with the note, and left id 3 alone.
- Full suite 611 of 612 (`BuildStampTest` fails in a worktree, also on `main`), Pint and PHPStan pass.
params.title: The same forward twice is one mail
